title: Candy Corn Bag

drivers.name: Halloween (event week)
drivers.evidence: Noise-adjusted x2.65 vs baseline from 2 past occurrences (2024, 2025); consistent with 2023.

drivers.name: TikTok trend
drivers.evidence: New driver; no prior data; plausible uplift but uncertain; shrunk toward 1.0.

drivers.name: Price increase (+6%)
drivers.evidence: Minor price rise; past promotions show 10-30% off still boosted sales; likely minor downside.

adjustment.analysis: Halloween drives a strong, consistent uplift (noise-adjusted x2.65). The price increase to $4.08 (+6%) is modest and unlikely to offset demand. TikTok trend is a new driver with limited evidence; it may amplify Halloween effect but lacks historical support. The classical model's x2.65 is well-supported by past Halloween data. No evidence of pantry loading or supply risk. The baseline already reflects seasonal trends. No need to adjust spreads beyond baseline uncertainty.

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: Holiday: Halloween (Sat)
  shelf price: 4.08 (+6.0% vs regular price 3.85)
  planner notes: Product is trending on TikTok

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 10.3 | 5%-95%: 0.0 - 24.2 | 10%-90%: 0.0 - 19.0

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-85% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
